subtitle: When Kannauj Became the Measure of Kings

panels.shot: sweeping wide shot of Kannauj’s riverfront, three kings in separate planes facing the city
panels.action: Nagabhata II, Dharmapala, and Govinda III stand apart on different ridges overlooking the distant sprawl of Kannauj by the Ganga, each in full regal armour and robes, each reaching toward the city with a different gesture of claim.

dialogue.text: In the age after Harsha, three distant kings turned to one river city—Kannauj—knowing that its throne could make or unmake their claim to rule North India.

i18n.hi: हर्ष के बाद के युग में, दूर–दूर के तीन राजा एक नदी नगर कन्नौज पर नज़र गड़ाए थे—जानते थे, इसका तख्त ही उनके उत्तर भारत के हक़ को बना या मिटा सकता है।

panels.shot: dramatic aerial over ruined palace complex
panels.action: A bird’s-eye view of Kannauj’s old palace district lies quiet and partly in ruins, broken pillars and overgrown courtyards bathed in late-afternoon light; the Ganga curves beyond, busy with boats and trade.

dialogue.text: Since Harsha’s death in 647, Kannauj had drifted from empire’s capital to prize for rival clans, its broken halls still whispering of a time when one throne meant command over the north.

i18n.hi: ६४७ में हर्ष की मौत के बाद, कन्नौज साम्राज्य की राजधानी से प्रतिद्वंदी कुलों की दौलत बन गया, टूटी हवेलियाँ अब भी फुसफुसाती थीं उस दौर की जब एक ही तख्त से पूरे उत्तर को हुक्म मिलता था।

panels.shot: split-panel style composition, three medium shots arranged in one frame
panels.action: The frame is divided into three vertical bands: Nagabhata II in Malwa’s rocky plains reviewing cavalry, Dharmapala in Bengal beside a monastery and river boats, and Govinda III in the Deccan amid basalt forts and elephant corps, each shown in vigorous command.

dialogue.text: By the late eighth century, three powers had risen far from Kannauj—Gurjara-Pratihara in Malwa, Pala along the eastern Ganga, and Rashtrakuta in the Deccan—each now strong enough to lift its eyes to Harsha’s old seat.

i18n.hi: आठवीं सदी के आखिर तक, कन्नौज से दूर तीन ताकतें उठीं—मालवा में गुर्जर–प्रतिहार, पूरब की गंगा किनारे पाल, और दक्षिण में दक्कन के राश्ट्रकूट—अब इतने मज़बूत कि हर्ष की पुरानी गद्दी पर नज़र उठा सकें।

panels.shot: close three-quarter view on a spread of maps and royal hands
panels.action: On a wooden table lies a rough cloth map of northern India; three ghosted hands overlay in montage—Nagabhata II’s pointing toward the upper Ganga, Dharmapala’s resting over Bengal and Bihar, Govinda III’s hovering from the south toward Malwa and beyond.

dialogue.text: Their scribes called them protectors of realms, upholders of dharma, lords of elephants and cavalry—but to make such words ring true over the north, each court knew, a king must be seen in Kannauj.

i18n.hi: उनके लेखक उन्हें लोक–रक्षक, धर्म–पालक, हाथी–घुड़सवारों के स्वामी कहते रहे—पर उत्तर में इन बातों को सच्चा करने के लिए, हर दरबार जानता था, राजा को कन्नौज में देखा जाना ज़रूरी है।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a dim royal record hall
panels.action: In a shadowy hall lined with palm-leaf bundles, three illuminated scenes appear like visions: Nagabhata II conferring with ministers, Dharmapala with Brahmins and monks, Govinda III with generals and Jain preceptors, all in serious counsel.

dialogue.text: Their inscriptions speak in polished boasts, not in doubts. But between the lines we can hear the question that drove them: who would be acknowledged, by allies and rivals alike, as the paramount power of the north?

i18n.hi: शिलालेखों में चमकदार शेखी है, शक नहीं। पर पंक्तियों के बीच से जो सवाल सुनाई देता है, वही उन्हें चला रहा था: कौन माना जाएगा, दोस्त और दुश्मन दोनों की नज़रों में, उत्तर का सरताज हाकिम?

panels.shot: slow push-in on Dharmapala seated in assembly, slight low angle
panels.action: Dharmapala sits on a throne beneath a canopy in a grand open pavilion, courtiers and feudatory chiefs arranged in rows before him; beyond arches, the skyline of Kannauj rises, suggesting his presence in the city.

dialogue.text: Pala records like the Khalimpur plate tell of Dharmapala convening a great assembly at Kannauj, where northern chiefs, from the Ganga’s middle plains to the fringes of the Deccan, are said to have accepted his suzerainty.

i18n.hi: पाल अभिलेख, जैसे खलीमपुर ताम्रपत्र, बताते हैं कि धर्मपाल ने कन्नौज में महा–सभा बुलवाई, जहाँ गंगा के मध्यम मैदानों से लेकर दक्कन की सरहदों तक के उत्तर के सरदारों ने उसके आधिपत्य को मान लिया।

panels.shot: medium shot side-on to Dharmapala and a line of feudatories
panels.action: Dharmapala turns toward a line of lesser kings and chiefs, some with folded hands, others with wary faces; the setting is formal and austere, pillars framing the space like a court of ritual acknowledgment.

dialogue.text: “Stand as friends under Pala shelter,” Dharmapala says, “and the Ganga’s path will be guarded.”

i18n.hi: “पाल की छाँव में दोस्त बनो,” धर्मपाल कहता है, “तो गंगा की राह सुरक्षित रहेगी।”

panels.shot: cut to a different court, medium shot on a Rashtrakuta inscription being carved
panels.action: At a fortified Deccan capital, a stone slab lies propped as an artisan chisels Sanskrit lines; Govinda III stands nearby with his commander, overlooking painted scenes of northern campaigns on the wall.

dialogue.text: Rashtrakuta texts, celebrating kings like Dhruva and Govinda III, answer with their own tale: Deccan armies riding north, humbling Pala and Pratihara rulers, then returning south laden with prestige and tribute.

i18n.hi: राश्ट्रकूट ग्रंथ, ध्रुव और गोविंद तृतीय जैसे राजाओं का जश्न मनाते हुए, अपना किस्सा सुनाते हैं: दक्कनी सेनाएँ उत्तर को चल पड़ती हैं, पाल और प्रतिहार राजाओं को झुका कर लौटती हैं, मान–मर्यादा और नज़राना लादे हुए।

panels.action: A stylized battlefield spreads across plains north of the Narmada, lines of Rashtrakuta cavalry facing distant standard-bearing forces that evoke Pala and Pratihara hosts; dust rises, but the image avoids direct combat, capturing tension before clash.

dialogue.text: The Rashtrakuta records speak of northern forays as proof that even the famed rulers beyond the Vindhyas could be checked and chastened, a warning that Kannauj’s circle of power was open to intervention from afar.

i18n.hi: राश्ट्रकूट अभिलेख उत्तर के धावे को इस बात का सबूत बनाते हैं कि विंध्याचल के पार के मशहूर राजा भी रोके और सबक सिखाए जा सकते हैं—चेतावनी कि कन्नौज का शक्ति–चक्र दूर से दख़ल के लिए खुला है।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Nagabhata II studying reports by lamplight
panels.action: Nagabhata II sits in a stone-walled chamber of a Malwa fortress at night, lamplight falling on scrolls and a rough sketch of the Ganga plain; a commander stands nearby, pointing toward Kannauj on the map.

dialogue.text: Meanwhile Nagabhata II, ruling from the west, recovered from earlier reverses and pushed eastward. His Baroda copper-plate, issued around 812, proudly notes conquests that brought him close to Kannauj’s orbit.

i18n.hi: उधर पश्चिम से राज कर रहे नागभटा द्वितीय ने पिछली हार से उबर कर पूरब की ओर धावा बोला। करीब ८१२ का उसका बड़ौदा ताम्रपत्र शान से उन विजयों का बखान करता है, जिन्होंने उसे कन्नौज की परिधि के क़रीब ला खड़ा किया।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Pratihara march through Malwa toward the Ganga
panels.action: Nagabhata II rides at the head of a disciplined Pratihara column—horses, spearmen, and standard-bearers—moving from rocky Malwa terrain into greener riverine plains, the horizon suggesting the direction of Kannauj.

dialogue.text: “We ride not just for land,” Nagabhata murmurs to his general, “but for a seat that all must acknowledge.”

i18n.hi: “हम सिर्फ ज़मीन के लिए नहीं चढ़ते,” नागभटा अपने सेनापति से बुदबुदाता है, “उस आसन के लिए, जिसे सब मानें।”

panels.shot: intercut montage of three courts issuing grants
panels.action: Three separate scenes share the frame: Dharmapala placing his seal on a copper-plate, Nagabhata II doing the same in Malwa, and Govinda III in the Deccan; scribes bend over palm leaves and copper sheets, stylus poised.

dialogue.text: Each court set its version into copper and palm leaf: Dharmapala as lord of Kannauj’s assembly, Nagabhata as conqueror and protector, Govinda as chastiser of northern kings. The struggle lived as much in written memory as on the ground.

i18n.hi: हर दरबार ने अपनी कथा ताँबे और ताड़पत्र पर दर्ज करवाई: धर्मपाल कन्नौज सभा का स्वामी, नागभटा विजेता–रक्षक, गोविंद उत्तर के राजाओं को सबक सिखाने वाला। जंग ज़मीन पर जितनी चली, उतनी ही लिखी यादों में जिए।

panels.shot: wide shot over the Ganga valley showing shifting banners at city gates
panels.action: Viewed from a hill, the walls and gates of Kannauj are seen in temporal montage: different royal banners—Pala, Pratihara, and a suggestion of local powers—rising and falling over time as traders and pilgrims keep moving along the river.

dialogue.text: Archaeology and texts together suggest no single enduring hold. Control of Kannauj’s throne shifted, sometimes under Pala shading, sometimes under Pratihara reach, while Rashtrakuta pressure from the south kept both uneasy.

i18n.hi: पुरातत्व और ग्रंथ दोनों मिलकर बताते हैं कि किसी का टिकाऊ कब्ज़ा न रहा। कन्नौज की गद्दी कभी पाल की छाँव, कभी प्रतिहार की पहुँच में रही, जबकि दक्षिण से राश्ट्रकूट का दबाव दोनों को बेचैन रखता था।

panels.shot: medium shot in a quiet palace corridor, three kings as distant silhouettes
panels.action: In a dim corridor lined with carved pillars, three silhouettes pass at different depths—Dharmapala fading down one end, Govinda III turning away another, Nagabhata II advancing toward a balcony overlooking the plains.

dialogue.text: Modern historians call it a ‘Tripartite Struggle’. The actors themselves knew it as campaigns, retreats, councils, and gestures of recognition—moments when presence or absence at Kannauj quietly altered a king’s rank in the northern order.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार इसे ‘त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष’ कहते हैं। उस वक़्त के किरदारों के लिए यह अभियान, पीछे हटना, सभाएँ और मान–स्वीकार के इशारे थे—ऐसे पल, जब कन्नौज में मौजूद या ग़ैर–हाज़िर होना चुपचाप किसी राजा की हैसियत बदल देता था।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a courtly ritual in Kannauj’s royal courtyard
panels.action: In Kannauj’s central courtyard, Brahmins, monks, and officers stand as a king—left deliberately unspecific—performs a royal consecration beside a fire altar, while watching dignitaries from distant regions look on.

dialogue.text: As Daud Ali notes, sovereignty was performed: through gifts, rituals, and the sight of lesser lords attending a king in a city like Kannauj. The city’s meaning lay not only in walls and markets, but in the theatre of power staged there.

i18n.hi: जैसा कि दाऊद अली लिखते हैं, सत्ता दिखाई जाती थी: नेमतों, अनुष्ठानों, और कन्नौज जैसे नगर में छोटे राजाओं की हाज़िरी से। शहर की अहमियत सिर्फ दीवारों और बाज़ारों में नहीं, बल्कि वहाँ खेले गए ताकत के रंगमंच में थी।

panels.shot: medium shot on scholars comparing inscriptions at a modern desk
panels.action: A present-day scholarly setting shows open volumes of Epigraphia Indica, photographs of the Baroda and Khalimpur plates, and maps; a researcher’s hand traces routes from Bengal, Malwa, and the Deccan toward Kannauj.

dialogue.text: Cross-reading the Baroda copper-plate, the Khalimpur grant, and Rashtrakuta records, historians like R.C. Majumdar piece together the contest—each inscription magnifying its patron’s glory, yet together revealing a shifting balance without one final conqueror.

i18n.hi: बड़ौदा ताम्रपत्र, खलीमपुर दान–पत्र और राश्ट्रकूट अभिलेखों को साथ–साथ पढ़कर, आर. सी. मजुमदार जैसे इतिहासकार इस मुक़ाबले को जोड़ते हैं—हर शिलालेख अपने राजा की महिमा बढ़ाता है, पर साथ मिलकर एक ऐसी बदलती तसवीर दिखाता है जिसमें कोई आख़िरी विजेता नहीं।

panels.shot: high sunset wide over Kannauj and the Ganga, kings as faded superimposed figures
panels.action: At sunset the Ganga glows beside Kannauj’s spread of houses, temples, and ghats; faint, semi-transparent images of Nagabhata II, Dharmapala, and Govinda III hover above the horizon, fading into the landscape.

dialogue.text: In time, each king’s claim dimmed, but Kannauj’s lesson endures: a single city, once charged with prestige and memory, can become the test by which distant powers measure themselves—and the stage on which their rivalry is etched for history.

i18n.hi: वक़्त के साथ हर राजा का दावा धुंधला पड़ गया, पर कन्नौज की सीख बची रही: कोई एक शहर, जब प्रतिष्ठा और याद से भर जाए, तो दूर–दराज़ ताकतें खुद को उसी से तौलने लगती हैं—और उनकी टक्कर की लकीरें इतिहास पर उसी के मंच पर उभर जाती हैं।
